claims.disproof_condition: Downgrade if Meta's CPO evaluation ends without fleet adoption (subsequent OCP/engineering disclosures choosing pluggables/other vendors), or if reliability claims fail to replicate at fleet scale; upgrade when the canonical ECOC 2025 paper full text is obtained, or Meta/another hyperscaler announces volume CPO deployment with Broadcom.
claims.statement: Customer-side corroboration for Broadcom's CPO position: Meta researchers' own ECOC 2025 paper reports operating 15 Bailly 51.2T CPO switches past 1 million device hours with zero link flaps — self-described as the highest system-level device hours reported for CPO — with lower-bound optical-link MTBF sufficient for a 24K GPU AI cluster at >90% training efficiency, and 65% lower power per 100G lane versus retimed pluggables. This is the hyperscaler customer naming and quantifying Broadcom's CPO in production-representative operation, upgrading an edge previously supported only by Broadcom self-report. Limits: 15-switch trial scale, not fleet deployment; Meta's concurrently announced Minipack3N is non-CPO (Spectrum-4), so CPO remains in evaluation not standard; quotes carried by trade press — canonical ECOC paper full text not yet public (upgrade trigger).

source_doc.title: Meta ECOC 2025 Bailly CPO deployment paper (verbatim via The Next Platform, 2025-10-17)

sources.quote: Over the first 1 million device hours with the Bailly switches...there were zero link flaps observed.
To the best of our knowledge, this is the highest device hours reported for CPO technology operation at the system level.

The demonstrated lower bound mean time between failures of (MTBFs) of optical links can readily support a 24K GPU AI cluster with >90 percent training efficiency without interconnect failures being the bottleneck.
the Bailly CPO switch optics delivered 65 percent lower power per 100 Gb/sec lane compared to retimed pluggable optical models.
